To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) we can learn a sparse generative model that forecasts human daily activity with few demonstrations, (ii) we can continuously learn a generative model of human daily activity from a single demonstration, (iii) we can learn an adaptive generative model of driving behavior from a large dataset, and (iv) we can learn incentivized predictive state representations that help an artificial agent perform a task better.

(1) We can learn a policy that forecasts agent futures from demonstrations of agent behavior, (2) We can learn an agent policy that forecasts human futures in the real world from demonstrations of agent and human behavior, (3) We can learn agent policies that forecast human and agent futures in realistic driving domains, and (4) We can learn predictive state representations to perform a task in the presence of other agents.

(1) sparse models can generalize from few demonstrations to predict agent behavior, (2) adaptive models can continuously learn to predict human daily activity from demonstrations, (3) high-dimensional generative forecasting models can learn to predict human driving behavior from demonstrations, (4) incentivized forecasting can be used to learn predictive state representation, and (5) the forecasting framework can be extended to multiagent domains.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of forecasting systems for the future behavior of agents.
the problem of forecasting agent behavior.
the design of learning systems that are capable of forecasting future behavior of agents.
